s.d: the traditional dress of Vietnamese women consisting of a tunic with long sleeves and panels front and back; the tunic is worn over trousers
A two panelled dress, worn by Vietnamese women as a national costume.
a verb tense in some languages (classical Greek and Sanskrit) expressing action (especially past action) without indicating its completion or continuation
A verb paradigm found in certain languages, usually an unmarked form or one that expresses the perfective or aorist aspect.
A particular verb in the aorist.
Of or pertaining to a verb in the aorist aspect.

aorta.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀορτή (aortḗ, “the arteries springing from the heart”), from ἀορτέω (aortéō), lengthened form of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift, raise”).

s.d: the large trunk artery that carries blood from the left ventricle of the heart to branch arteries
The great artery which carries the blood from the heart to all parts of the body except the lungs; the main trunk of the arterial system.
(figuratively) The liveliest part of something.
x: Tracing their battles, I had many occasions to walk along Second Avenue, the aorta of the Lower East Side, exploring places that were once as vibrant and tumultuous as Midtown Manhattan.

aortic.e: From aorta + -ic. By surface analysis, aort- + -ic.

s.d: of or relating to the aorta
Of or pertaining to the aorta or the aortic valve.
an aneurysm of the aorta
the part of the aorta that arches and turns downward
The curving portion of the aorta that bends between the ascending aorta and the descending aorta, from which the brachiocephalic artery, left carotid artery, and left subclavian artery arise.

One of a series of six paired embryonic vascular structures which connect the ventral arterial system lying anterior to the heart to the dorsal arterial system above the digestive tract, persist in adult fishes but are reduced or much modified in the adult of higher forms, and give rise to the great arteries of the neck and head.
the final section of the aortic arch; a narrowing of the aorta as a result of decreased blood flow when in foetal life.
the orifice from the lower left chamber of the heart to the aorta
a plexus of lymph nodes in the lower portion of the abdominal aorta
abnormal narrowing of the aortic valve
a semilunar valve between the left ventricle and the aorta; prevents blood from flowing from the aorta back into the heart
inflammation of the aorta

aoudad.e: From French aoudad, from Tashelhit awdad.

s.d: wild sheep of northern Africa
The Barbary sheep, Ammotragus lervia.
x: In captivity the aoudad seems to like water and to enjoy taking a bath. The diet consists of grass, herbaceous plants, and stunted bushes.
